theme.title: Rotation: Growth → Value & Defensives
theme.summary: Health Care (+2.50%) and Consumer Staples (+2.22%) led the market today, while Technology (-2.92%) and Communication Svcs (-1.28%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -1.58% versus +1.49% for defensives and -0.27% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained -0.09% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -1.88%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -1.93%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX rose 10.48% to 16.87, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 1.44% to $4,125.10, crude oil was little changed at $94.86, and bitcoin slipped 2.01% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
